story_type: missile defense interceptor destroys a target missile at night
hook: A cargo jet dropped a missile. Alaska fired back.
narration: A target missile was screaming in over the Pacific, and this launcher in Alaska fired back.
It started with an Air Force C-17, which dropped a medium-range target missile out over the ocean.
It fell under parachutes, then its rocket motor lit.
In Kodiak, Alaska, a THAAD launcher fired an interceptor into the night.
[short pause] THAAD carries no explosive warhead. It destroys its target by slamming straight into it.
outcome: THAAD detected, tracked and intercepted the target in a successful missile defense test.
title: THAAD hits a missile dropped from a C-17
description:
On July 30, 2017, the Missile Defense Agency and soldiers of the 11th Air Defense Artillery Brigade intercepted a medium-range target missile, air-launched by a C-17 over the Pacific, with a THAAD interceptor fired from Kodiak, Alaska.

question_comment: Would you have guessed a missile could hit another missile with no warhead?

facts.claim: MDA and 11th ADA Brigade soldiers conducted a successful THAAD test
facts.source_quote: The U.S. Missile Defense Agency and U.S. Army soldiers of the 11th Air Defense Artillery Brigade from Fort Bliss, Texas, conducted a successful missile defense test today using the Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) system.

facts.claim: A medium-range target missile was air-launched by a C-17 over the Pacific
facts.source_quote: A medium-range target ballistic missile (MRBM) was air-launched by a U.S. Air Force C-17 over the Pacific Ocean.

facts.claim: THAAD at Kodiak, Alaska detected, tracked and intercepted the target
facts.source_quote: The THAAD weapon system located at Pacific Spaceport Complex Alaska in Kodiak, Alaska, detected, tracked and intercepted the target.
